notes: TBox revision. The rule defines substitutes (positive cross-price elasticity), so it has no exceptions; the revision swaps substitutes for complements, a common confusion and clearly false. Derivability very_unlikely: stated directly. The three derived queries name invented pairs (two colas, two bus companies, two oat milk brands) and state in the prompt that they are substitutes, so the rule is the only route (inheritance, 2 hops). Real textbook pairs (coffee and tea, butter and margarine) are not asked: the model may hold their price effect by name, and the audit showed three models calling coffee and tea complements. The third is an application: a production plan. Migration (2026-11-11): the two indeterminate coffee/tea and butter/margarine queries and their worlds were dropped (TBox is determinate only); the Spanish question, which three models answered "disminuye" (likely reading it as the good's own demand), now spells out "the goods that can replace it"; a conjunction was added. Near unrelated: complements, the neighbouring concept; its reference differs from the new answer.
